messages:
alex_m: FYI we had a brief outage window this morning when a batch of spot GPUs in us-west-2 got interrupted. Observed ~3m degraded throughput for inference workers.
sarah_w: Did we get termination notices? provider/region?
alex_m: Yep - AWS spot in us-west-2. termination notices arrived, node-termination-handler annotated nodes, but cluster-autoscaler still removed node objects before replacements were Ready. Race between cordon/drain and CA scale-down.
miguel: Can you outline the sequence? good to know exact ordering.
alex_m: Sequence we traced: 1) EC2 2-min interruption notice -> NTH annotates. 2) lifecycle controller attempted cordon+taint (redwood/preemptible=evict). 3) We request warm replacement but instance not yet registered. 4) CA sees node as unneeded or the ASG recently updated and deletes node object -> pods rescheduled but some stateful pods hit volume detach timeouts and failed over.
sarah_w: So CA and our lifecycle choreography are racing. Two clear knobs: block CA from deleting nodes during preemptible eviction flow, and accelerate replacement launch (warm pool or immediate ASG scale).
nate: CA already honors cluster-autoscaler.k8s.io/scale-down-disabled annotation. We can set that when we detect a preemptible notice. Also bump --scale-down-unneeded-time for gpu nodegroups to reduce aggressive kills.
miguel: Implementation pattern idea: make preemptible eviction a 2-phase process: preparing -> terminal. Controller adds annotation redwood/preemptible-evict=preparing + cluster-autoscaler.k8s.io/scale-down-disabled=true; then trigger warm-replacement (increase warm pool or ASG desired), wait for Ready; then flip to terminal and allow final drain. If replacement fails to appear after timeout, remove the scale-down-disabled so CA can reclaim to avoid stuck capacity.
sarah_w: We should also add tolerationSeconds on workloads to allow short graceful shutdowns. Example toleration for apps that can checkpoint quickly:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: model-worker
spec:
  tolerations:
    - key: "redwood/preemptible"
      operator: "Exists"
      effect: "NoExecute"
      tolerationSeconds: 300 # tolerate 5m
```
This buys time while replacement spins up.
alex_m: Controller prototype flow we tested:
1) NTH sees notice -> POST /lifecycle/v1/preemptible {node, asg} to controller
2) controller annotates node: cluster-autoscaler.k8s.io/scale-down-disabled=true and sets label redwood/draining=true
3) controller triggers warm-pool bump for ASG via AWS API
4) wait for new instance to register + kubelet Ready
5) switch annotation to redwood/preemptible-evict=terminal, remove scale-down-disabled and perform final drain
This prevented CA from deleting the node mid-eviction.
miguel: Useful cli for locking node from CA:
```bash
kubectl annotate node/$NODE cluster-autoscaler.k8s.io/scale-down-disabled=true --overwrite
```
And cordon+taint:
```bash
kubectl cordon $NODE
kubectl taint node $NODE redwood/preemptible=evict:NoSchedule
```
nate: Other CA tuning: set --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true for GPU pools, set --scale-down-unneeded-time=600s for gpu nodegroups, and ensure CA version is modern (upgrade to 1.26 in us-west-2 to get better mixed-instance/surge behavior).
infra-bot: noticed: cluster-autoscaler on us-west-2 clusters is 1.24. Plan upgrade to 1.26 during next maintenance window.
sarah_w: Cost/benefit: warm pool increases short-term spend but avoids p99 latency spikes and retries which can cost more. For expensive GPU types, small warm pools per ASG are worth the SLAs.
miguel: Edge case: quota prevents replacement instances from launching. Controller should implement fallback: after 12m without replacement, remove scale-down-disabled so CA can reclaim and emit pager alert.
alex_m: We'll add a timeout and alerting. Also add metrics: preemptible_event_count, replacement_latency_seconds, p99_latency_before_after and cost_delta. I'll attach graphs in the PR.
sarah_w: Action items:
- [ ] prototype lifecycle-controller (miguel)
- [ ] add tolerationSeconds + review PDBs for critical pods (sarah)
- [ ] patch CA tuning for gpu nodegroups and test (nate)
- [ ] staging canary for mass preemption (alex)
- [ ] add timeout fallback + pager if replacement fails (miguel)

alex_m: I'll open a small PR (300-400 LOC) with the controller + lambda glue and example pod tolerations. Will include unit tests and an integration run in staging.

miguel: When you have the PR link ping here. Also include runbook steps for oncall to manually flip scale-down-disabled if controller is unhealthy.

alex_m: Good call. Will add a one-click kubectl snippet to the runbook.

deploybot: canary scheduled: staging preemptible flow test on 2026-03-25T03:00Z.
infra-bot: reminder: add a canary metric for 'replacement_registered' to detect ASG failures early.

alex_m: Thanks everyone. I'll post updates in this thread as PR and metrics land.
